\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بسنت} (basant)}{بسنت (basant)}]{\ur{بسنت} (basant) — the spring kite festival}

\label{lesson:UR-C319-basant}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for congratulations, then the Urdu for to cling.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بسنت}}
\textbf{\ur{بسنت}} — \emph{basant} — \textquotedblleft{}the spring kite festival\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{لاہور} \ur{میں} \ur{بسنت} \ur{کا} \ur{میلہ} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Lāhaur meṅ basant kā melā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a spring kite fair in Lahore.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بسنت}} (\emph{basant}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{vasanta}, \textquotedblleft{}spring\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams). In Lahore it names the day of kites at the end of winter.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{basant}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{basant}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Lāhaur meṅ basant kā melā thā.} — There was a spring kite fair in Lahore.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for congratulations, then the Urdu for to cling, then say \emph{basant} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بسنت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The spring kite festival\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

Before the new one: say the Urdu for to cling, then the Urdu for the spring kite festival.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چرخی} (charkhī)}{چرخی (charkhī)}]{\ur{چرخی} (charkhī) — a spool (for kite string)}

\label{lesson:UR-C319-charkhi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the spring kite festival, then the Urdu for a kite string.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چرخی}}
\textbf{\ur{چرخی}} — \emph{charkhī} — \textquotedblleft{}a spool (for kite string)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بھائی} \ur{نے} \ur{چرخی} \ur{پکڑی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bhāī ne charkhī pakṛī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother held the spool.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{چرخی}} (\emph{charkhī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{charkh}, \textquotedblleft{}a wheel\textquotedblright{}, with the small ending \emph{-ī}: the little wheel the string winds on.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اڑانا} (uṛānā)}{اڑانا (uṛānā)}]{\ur{اڑانا} (uṛānā) — to fly a kite; to make fly}

\label{lesson:UR-C319-urana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a kite string, then the Urdu for a spool.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اڑانا}}
\textbf{\ur{اڑانا}} — \emph{uṛānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to fly a kite; to make fly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہم} \ur{نے} \ur{چھت} \ur{پر} \ur{پتنگ} \ur{اڑائی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ham ne chhat par patang uṛāī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We flew a kite on the roof.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{پتنگ} \ur{اڑائی}, \emph{us ne patang uṛāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اڑانا}} (\emph{uṛānā}) is the causing partner of \textbf{\ur{اڑنا}}, to fly: CDIAL lists Hindi \emph{uṛānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to cause to fly\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{uḍḍīyatē} (CDIAL 1697).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کٹنا} (kaṭnā)}{کٹنا (kaṭnā)}]{\ur{کٹنا} (kaṭnā) — to be cut; to be cut loose}

\label{lesson:UR-C319-katna-cut-loose}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a spool, then the Urdu for to fly a kite.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{کٹنا}} — \emph{kaṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be cut; to be cut loose\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{شام} \ur{کو} \ur{میری} \ur{پتنگ} \ur{کٹ} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shām ko merī patang kaṭ gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the evening my kite was cut loose.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{پتنگ} \ur{کٹ} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh patang kaṭ gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کٹنا}} (\emph{kaṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousins \emph{kaṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be cut\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{kāṭnā} under Sanskrit \emph{kártati} (CDIAL 2854). It is the partner of \textbf{\ur{کاٹنا}}: you \textbf{\ur{کاٹنا}} a string, and a kite \textbf{\ur{کٹ} \ur{گئی}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shām ko merī patang kaṭ gaī.} — In the evening my kite was cut loose.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a spool, then the Urdu for to fly a kite, then say \emph{kaṭnā} again
\end{itemize}
